findings.title: Memory-recall 27.4% hit rate decomposed: intent-pollution fix alone caps the surface at ~36% best-case — floor math + corpus are the co-dominant miss cause; and 100% of recall benefit accrues to 'main' (zero sub-agent rows in 281), so the agent layer is fully memory-blind

evidence.quote:
Before starting implementation tasks, agents (kraken, architect, phoenix,
spark) should check the archival memory for relevant prior learnings.

findings.telemetry: 281 rows; hit 27.4% (~77 hits); pollution 24.6% (69 rows); by_source empty 154 / db 127 (zero 'local' rows — corroborates D3b-03/06 dead local arm); p50 top_score=0; by_subagent: main 281/281
findings.observe_how: Deterministic arithmetic on the harvest table: even if all 69 polluted rows are misses, best-case clean hit rate = 77/(281-69) = 36.3% — so intent sanitization alone recovers <=9pp of the 72.6% miss rate; the remaining ~135 clean-intent misses sit with the HYBRID_FLOOR math (D3b-01/08) and corpus coverage. p50 top_score=0 means the MEDIAN per-prompt recall surfaces nothing scoreable. Confirm post-fix by re-running the harvest split: hit rate among non-polluted rows vs polluted rows, and watch for any non-'main' by_subagent entry (today there are none, despite agent-memory-recall.md mandating agent recall).

findings.title: Intel-bus is a monologue, not a multi-agent bus: all 318 live rows have agent=null (zero sub-agent attribution ever recorded), and corr-null 60.7% means rows cannot be joined into request flows — the §9 cohesion metrics and per-agent C.5 evidence are uncomputable from this log
findings.telemetry: live window: 318 rows over 7 distinct days, by_agent {null:318}; bus plumbing = 193 rows (bus_write 67 + agent_recall_bus_read 48 + memory_awareness_bus_read 42 + bus_read_latency 34 + bus_write_dropped 2); lifetime non-null agents are only 'main' (222, all memory_recall) and codex-adversary (4)
findings.observe_how: The arithmetic closes exactly: live null-specialist count (193) equals the sum of the five bus-plumbing query types, so every live row is either facade plumbing or a specialist call with NO agent identity attached. Combined with D4a-01 (correlation_id structurally inert — 60.7% null and the rest unjoinable), there is no way to answer 'which agent benefited from the bus' — the question C.5 and the §9 weekly digest exist to answer. Verify by grepping the live emitters in .claude/hooks/src/ and scripts/code-intel.mjs for any code path that sets an agent/subagent field on intel-bus rows; confirm absence, then add attribution at the SubagentStop/Task boundary before starting the C.3 watch (SEED-10), or the 4-week watch will collect 4 more weeks of unjoinable rows.

findings.title: Codegraph in-facade routing share is 45.7% (37 of 81 eligible queries) — the other 44 fell back to TLDR despite codegraph being 'LIVE'; on the only measurable axis, adoption is at barely half the >=80% C.5 gate, and the gate's true denominator (facade-vs-bypass) has zero data

evidence.quote: **C.5** (flip `CCV3_FACADE_MODE=deny`) is **gated** on intel-bus showing **≥80% facade-route adoption** + bypass→0

findings.telemetry: live window: codegraph-eligible queries = find-symbol 53 + who-calls 25 + code-context 3 = 81; specialists: codegraph 35 + codegraph-fused 2 = 37 vs tldr 43 + tldr-fused 1 = 44 (37+44=81, exact accounting) -> 45.7% codegraph share; only 7 distinct live days
findings.observe_how: Every live tldr row is a fallback for a codegraph-eligible query (no cfg/dfg/slice/dead/diagnostics query types appear in the live window), so the 54% fallback rate is not TLDR doing its own job — it is the kill-switch-order path (CCV3_KILLSWITCH -> CCV3_CODEGRAPH_OFF -> binary-absent -> TLDR) firing on more than half of calls. Investigate WHICH leg fires: instrument the fallback branch in scripts/code-intel.mjs to log the fallback reason (env flag vs binary-absent vs missing .codegraph DB in the query cwd) to intel-bus, then re-measure. Separately, the C.5 gate as written (facade-route adoption vs bypass) remains unmeasurable per D1b-01 — 37 codegraph rows over 7 days cannot evidence an 80% gate whose denominator is never logged.

findings.title: Agent-recall telemetry shows the working agent fleet is ~8 of 36: 30 agents (incl. oracle, debug-agent, sleuth, architect, phoenix, arbiter — the agents the rules route to) have NEVER hit the recall surface; activity is dominated by the review pipeline (codex-adversary+critic+plan-reviewer = 39/78 = 50%), and banned 'Explore' appears 8 times

evidence.quote: For codebase exploration tasks, use `scout` (Sonnet) instead of `Explore` (Haiku).

findings.telemetry: 78 rows: codex-adversary 23, scout 16, kraken 12, critic 12, Explore 8, plan-reviewer 4, Plan 2, spark 1; agents_never_appearing = 30/36 (incl. all debug/research/deploy/orchestration agents)
findings.observe_how: Two readings, both actionable: (1) if the 30 absent agents are never spawned, the 36-agent inventory advertised in CLAUDE.md/agent docs is ~78% dead weight — maintenance cost (model-selection rules, validation hooks, docs) with no usage; cross-check by grepping Task-tool spawn telemetry (Braintrust traces) for any spawn of the 30 names over the same window. (2) If they ARE spawned but never reach agent-recall-injector, the injector's matcher misses them (consistent with D2b-01 Agent/Task matcher split-brain). Either way the surface is double-dead: per D2b-03 the injector yielded 0 memories in all 78 fires that DID happen. The 8 'Explore' rows are a live violation of use-scout-not-explore.md observable directly in telemetry — a cheap compliance probe for any future rules-adherence check. Recommend: prune or archive never-used agents, or fix injector coverage, before investing further in per-agent memory.

findings.title: Codex-lift telemetry inverts the review pipeline's assumed hierarchy (codex_only 77 > claude_only 49, overlap only 14/140) — the single cross-model pass out-finds the multi-agent Claude review arm, the 'both-flag = high-confidence' synthesis rule almost never has material (1.4 findings/run), and the log tracks raw counts with no accepted/rejected disposition, so the designed ROI decision cannot actually be made from it

evidence.quote: The `codex_only` count IS the cross-model lift — if it's consistently zero, the Codex pass isn't earning its quota cost and should be reconsidered.
Findings that BOTH critic and codex-adversary flag are high-confidence - the cross-model lift is exactly the findings only one side catches.

findings.telemetry: 10 runs: claude_only 49, codex_only 77, both 14 (overlap = 10% of 140 distinct findings; both averages 1.4/run)
findings.observe_how: The rule's own kill-criterion (codex_only consistently zero) is decisively NOT met — Codex earns its quota on this metric. But the inverse comparison is the real signal: a single gpt-5.5 pass produces 57% more unique findings than the parallel Opus critic+plan-reviewer arm. Three non-exclusive explanations the current schema cannot distinguish: Claude reviewers under-detect; finding granularity/dedup differs per source (one side splits, the other merges); or Codex over-reports unvalidated noise. Fix is one schema field: extend the codex-lift.jsonl row (emitted by /review and /premortem per codex-adversarial.md §Telemetry) with per-source accepted/rejected disposition recorded at synthesis time, then ROI = accepted-codex_only per quota-dollar becomes computable. Until then, treat 77-vs-49 as a precision-unknown count, not a verdict that the Claude review arm is redundant.
